title: Auto bus stops and demand
text: Auto bus lines show 400 m and every street stop, but demand counts a stop only about every 2 km, so an Auto line gets about a fifth fewer riders than stops placed 400 m apart (2,814 against 3,580 a day on a 3.7 km NYC line). Keep it as is (my pick: players can step to 600 m or place stops), or count every Auto stop for demand, which changes riders on every Auto line in every save? T-3924.

title: BRT design answers
text: Five questions in artifacts/trainworld/review/brt-design.md (T-3378). Picks: BRT stations for BRT lines only; 60 buses an hour a lane, lines cut to fit; off-road busway US$25M a km at 60 km/h; plain buses stay in traffic in town; keep 35 km/h, 18 s at a station, US$2M a station.

title: Station upgrade upkeep rate
text: Station upgrades now cost 0.1% of their price a day (waiting room US$5k, park and ride US$20k; T-3922). It barely deters spam on a rich network. Keep 0.1%, or raise to 0.25% like tram stops (my pick)?

title: Tram braking value
text: Trams brake at 0.8 m/s2, trains 0.9 (T-3921), so trams lose slightly more per stop; real trams brake harder (1.2-1.3). Keep 0.8 (my pick) or 0.9 so only the dwell changed?

title: Two workers on big saves
text: Lag survey (T-3917): on 2,000+ station saves the game runs one solving worker to save memory. Two workers would cut a load from 333 to 226 s and an edit's calculation from 296 to 188 s on the NA save, for +1.3-1.6 GB memory (desktop already 4.2-6.5 GB). Yes or no? I'd say no for now: build T-3925 and T-2624 first, which speed edits without more memory.

title: Read iPhone reporters' saves
text: Five iPhone players reported the page crashing right away (11-19 to 11-20). Reading their saved games on the server (T-3781's route) would show which game was loading. May we, one yes per account? Their report ids: 262cb413, 98429d29, 7130f860, 9705548e, fa20c413.
